key_insight: ROSE reframes NL2SQL evaluation around user intent: it judges a predicted SQL by whether it answers the natural-language question, not whether it matches a single ground-truth SQL. This makes evaluation robust to syntactic variation, ambiguous questions, and noisy labels.
problem_solved: Execution Accuracy (EX) is brittle: it penalizes semantically-equivalent SQL rewrites, ignores multiple valid interpretations of a question, and is easily misled by incorrect ground-truth SQL—leading to unreliable model evaluation.
method: Define an intent-centered evaluation objective that prioritizes whether the predicted SQL fulfills the natural-language question's intent rather than structural match to ground truth.

Compare predicted queries on the basis of their answers/semantics (e.g., execution/intent equivalence, handling multiple valid interpretations) to avoid penalizing syntactic differences and to tolerate noisy labels.
Incorporate mechanisms to detect and account for ambiguity and ground-truth errors so the metric reflects true user-facing correctness.
impact: ROSE gives researchers and engineers a more faithful, user-centric signal for NL2SQL model quality—improving model selection, error analysis, and dataset validation. It reduces false negatives from evaluation and encourages models that actually satisfy user intent.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison diagram: EX vs ROSE — same question, two different SQLs; EX marks one as wrong, ROSE marks both correct if they answer the intent.
Flowchart of ROSE evaluation: input question → predicted SQL → intent check/execute → pass/fail decision.
Bar chart showing divergence between EX and ROSE scores across models/datasets to highlight robustness gains.
Example panel: ambiguous question with multiple valid SQLs and annotated explanations showing how ROSE handles ambiguity and noisy ground-truth.
paper_title: ROSE: An Intent-Centered Evaluation Metric for NL2SQL
paper_authors: Wenqi Pei, Shizheng Hou, Boyan Li, Han Chen, Zhichao Shi
